title: Team runtime mode and adapter contract
description: Define Team runtime mode selection and the neutral adapter contract for real-agent, editor-subagent, and broker-only execution.
acceptance: Team runtime supports real-agent, editor-subagent, and broker-only modes.
Node.js remains the default runtime when no override is provided.
Adapter metadata is recorded even when broker-only mode disables actual spawn.
notes: 2026-06-18 | done | runtime mode and adapter contract closed in AI-Atomic-Framework; broker-only, real-agent, and editor-subagent mode contract landed as the runtime baseline.

title: Editor subagent bridge contract
description: Define the neutral bridge contract that lets editor-native subagents execute Team roles without becoming the governance authority.
acceptance: Editor-subagent execution preserves role, lease, artifact, and retry metadata.
Editor execution remains bounded by ATM allowedFiles and evidence rules.
notes: 2026-06-18 | done | editor subagent bridge contract closed in AI-Atomic-Framework; execution remains subordinate to ATM governance and preserves role-envelope metadata.

title: Team reviewer-validator rework route state machine
description: Turn reviewer and validator findings into explicit Team runtime route transitions such as needs-rework and revalidate-pending.
acceptance: Blocking reviewer or validator findings can formally move a Team run into needs-rework.
Route transitions are recorded as runtime state rather than advisory text only.
notes: 2026-06-18 | done | reviewer and validator rework routing closed in AI-Atomic-Framework; runtime transitions now capture needs-rework and revalidate-pending states.

title: Role artifact handoff and bounded retry contract
description: Define role-to-role artifact contracts and the bounded retry / escalation runtime budget for Team rework loops.
acceptance: Implementer, reviewer, validator, and evidence collector each declare required artifact surfaces.
Retry exhaustion escalates instead of looping forever.
notes: 2026-06-18 | done | artifact handoff and bounded retry contract closed in AI-Atomic-Framework; retry exhaustion now escalates instead of looping forever.

title: Node.js reference worker adapter and broker-only fallback
description: Ship the default Node.js Team worker adapter and the broker-only fallback path so ATM can run with or without spawned agents.
acceptance: Node.js worker runtime can execute without editor dependency.
Broker-only mode preserves governance checks without spawning agents.
notes: 2026-06-18 | done | Node.js worker adapter and broker-only fallback closed in AI-Atomic-Framework; Node.js remains the default Team runtime.

title: Python and C# reference worker adapter examples

notes: 2026-06-18 | done | Python and C# adapter examples closed in AI-Atomic-Framework; examples prove neutral runtime contract without replacing the Node.js default.

title: Vendor-neutral Team agent provider contract and orchestration kernel
description: Create the vendor-neutral Team runtime provider contract, registry, and orchestration kernel that all future SDK and editor bridges must use.
acceptance: Provider and orchestration contracts stay vendor-neutral.
Runtime core can register multiple providers without leaking vendor-specific branching into Team role orchestration.
Worker authority boundaries remain coordinator-owned.
notes: 2026-06-19 | planned | foundation card for the multi-vendor Team runtime lane opened from the integration blueprint.

title: Permission broker and configurable policy layer
description: Introduce a vendor-neutral permission broker so Team workers always run under ATM-managed policy and lease boundaries.
acceptance: File, tool, network, and vendor permissions are checked through one broker contract.
Policy can be configured per adopter repo without changing framework runtime code.
Provider bridges cannot grant themselves elevated rights.
notes: 2026-06-19 | planned | policy lane opened alongside the vendor-neutral runtime kernel.

title: Governed-repo vendor integration config surface
description: Define how adopter repositories provide vendor-specific Team runtime settings without putting those values inside the ATM framework repository.
acceptance: Adopter repos can place vendor config under a governed local directory.
ATM can discover, validate, and explain missing or malformed config.
Framework templates and docs show the expected config layout without embedding real secrets.
notes: 2026-06-19 | planned | governed-repo config lane opened to keep provider settings out of the ATM framework repo.

title: Cross-vendor observability and query log
description: Create one shared observability event model and query surface for Team workers across every vendor and execution mode.
acceptance: Team runtime emits one event schema for session start, step execution, tool invocation, artifact output, and completion or failure.
Operators can query by task, team run, provider, role, and artifact.
Event logging preserves governance evidence boundaries and redaction policy.
notes: 2026-06-19 | planned | observability lane opened as a first-class runtime contract, not a provider-specific afterthought.

title: Provider selection defaults and role overrides
description: Let Team runs choose a repo default provider while still allowing role-level overrides for implementer, reviewer, validator, planner, or other roles.

Individual roles can override provider, SDK, model, and runtime mode.
Selection decisions are recorded in the runtime contract and observability output.
notes: 2026-06-19 | planned | provider-selection lane opened to support mixed-vendor role assignments with deterministic fallback.
